Imported profiles must be trusted again before their scripts run
Refreshed window layout with more spacing on the dashboard

Reliability: build.rs fails hard on GResource compilation error
Reliability: mutex poisoning recovery in auto-switch background thread

Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion support for CSS animations

Accessibility: all dialogs now dismissible with Escape key
UX: removed author label from bottom-left corner
Argon2id key derivation for profile encryption (replaces raw SHA-256)
Random per-message salt added to every encrypted payload
Encryption passphrase is no longer persisted to disk
Config, cache, and log files set strict 0600/0700 permissions
Key material zeroed from memory on drop (zeroize)
Sandbox mode fails loudly when bwrap/firejail is missing
Ping and DNS input validated against injection
Proxy settings check for GNOME schema before applying
Regex DoS protection with size-limited compilation
Compiled regexes cached across auto-switch cycles
Watchdog and auto-switch blocking calls offloaded from UI thread
Update checker response body size-limited to 512 KiB
Tokio runtime features narrowed to reduce binary size
DEB/RPM packages now declare NetworkManager dependency
Bubblewrap uses existence check for /lib64 instead of hard bind
Schedule Profile Activation - Schedule entries now use real profiles from your configuration
Hotkey Profile Binding - Hotkeys can be bound to actual profiles for quick switching
Automatic Schedule Execution - Scheduler now properly activates profiles at scheduled times
VPN Disconnect Support - Disconnect from VPN connections when switching profiles
MTU Configuration - Set custom MTU values per interface
MAC Address Cloning - Configure cloned/spoofed MAC addresses
DNS Search Domains - Configure search domains for DNS resolution
Hostname Configuration - Set static and pretty hostnames via profiles
Timezone Configuration - Automatic timezone switching per profile
Default Printer Selection - Set default printer when activating profiles
Environment Variables - Configure environment variables per profile
Sandbox Script Execution - Run automation scripts in a bubblewrap or firejail sandbox
Profile Encryption - Encrypt sensitive profile data with AES-256-GCM

Automatic Update Check - Checks GitHub for newer releases on startup
What's New Section - Release notes visible in the About dialog
Improved Card Styling - Consistent shadow and border on all dashboard cards
Center-Aligned Icons - Navigation icons are properly centered when sidebar is collapsed

msgid: Learn how to use Network Manager

CD Network Manager is a comprehensive system and network profile manager for Linux. It allows you to create, manage, and quickly switch between different network and system configuration profiles. Perfect for users who need different settings for home, work, or different network environments.

The Dashboard provides an overview of your current network configuration. View your active network connections, IP addresses, and connection status. The active profile is displayed prominently, and you can quickly switch between profiles using the profile selector. Network statistics and connection health are updated in real-time.

Profiles are the core feature of Network Manager. Each profile stores a complete set of network and system settings including:

• Network configuration (IP, DNS, gateway)
• Proxy settings
• Firewall rules
• System services to enable/disable
• Custom scripts to run on activation

Create profiles for different locations or use cases, then switch between them with a single click. Profiles can be exported and imported for backup or sharing.

The Logs page shows network-related system events and profile switch history. View connection changes, profile activations, and any errors that occurred. Filter logs by type or search for specific events. Logs help you troubleshoot connectivity issues and track configuration changes over time.

The Settings page allows you to configure application preferences. Set the default profile to activate at startup, configure automatic profile switching based on network detection, enable or disable system tray integration, and customize notification preferences. Advanced options include daemon configuration and privilege settings.

Each profile can include:

• Static or DHCP IP configuration
• Custom DNS servers
• HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy settings
• Firewall zone assignment
• VPN connection settings
• System services to start/stop
• Pre/post activation scripts
• Network interface selection

• Create a 'Default' profile as a baseline configuration.
• Use descriptive profile names like 'Home WiFi' or 'Office Wired'.
• Test profiles before relying on them in critical situations.
• Export important profiles for backup.
• Use the system tray for quick profile switching.
• Check logs if a profile switch doesn't work as expected.
